premise: I used my late husband’s $112,000 life insurance to launch a vintage fountain pen restoration and nib‑grinding workshop with my stepson, securing a notarized 45% stake and a lifetime supply of ink for my journals; when a luxury pen brand offered $590,000 for the restored collection and client list he forged a dissolution, sold my share, and mailed me a $3,900 “inkwell” check—I retrieved our contract hidden inside the barrel of a 1920s Parker Duofold, proved the forgery, and now run ‘Nib of Deceit Pens,’ where he polishes nibs in a vest that reads ‘Written in Fraud’ and every gift box prints his perjury case number.
